Below is what an AI scientist wrote during a search in that world: its analysis at every round, in order, and the
name and hypothesis of the trial it ended with. Does the text, anywhere, state the rule?
- "yes": it states the rule's substance (what is changed and how).
- "partly": it identifies the right kind of change but not its specifics.
- "no": anything else.

## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
There are no trials yet. Earlier searches got 0 dev success and 0 training success across 84 trials, so the agent never finishes an exact build. That points to optimisation and inductive bias, not generalisation, so this round goes for breadth and stacking. Each of the 6 candidates combines PPO init hygiene: orthogonal weights, policy-output layers at gain 0.01 so the starting policy is near uniform, and a value layer at gain 1. Two ideas appear in all but one candidate. One is factorised logits: a per-type term, a per-anchor term and a per-type interaction. The other is a DONE head that reads global max pooling, so it can see whether any missing cell remains. The candidates differ in three ways. Heads: footprint convolutions, pooled statistics, a soft landing-layer gate, or a dense head. Trunks: a local column MLP, or a residual CNN with GroupNorm. Recipes: from 1 epoch with long rollouts and a high learning rate, to small batches with 3 epochs. Any score above 0 is the signal to follow up.

### Round 2
Every trial in round 1 scored 0 on dev and on training success. That includes stacks of init hygiene, GroupNorm, a raw-obs skip, factorised logits, footprint heads, dense heads, soft landing gates and sample-heavy recipes. So there is still no evidence for any idea. A failure mode no earlier trial addressed may explain all 90 zeros: DONE collapse. A random placement has negative expected reward, while DONE returns 0, so DONE's advantage early on (−V, roughly +0.5 to +2) is far larger than a correct brick's (about +0.09). High gamma, used in round 1, makes this worse. The policy likely learns to stop at once, and greedy evaluation then always scores 0. This round, every candidate makes DONE able to rise only slowly by scaling its output by a constant. The candidates differ in trunk and head (local footprint, flip/transpose symmetric head, everything-stack, starting net, 1-epoch sample-heavy, asymmetric evidence-gated DONE) and in recipe. Most use gamma 0.95 or lower.

### Round 3
Before round 2, all 84 trials and all 6 round-1 candidates scored 0 on dev and on training success. In round 2, the only nonzero results came from r2c2 (D4-symmetric shared head) and r2c3 (stack with a dense head), at 1/512 dev each. r2c3 also reached 0.0005 training success. Every round-2 candidate scaled DONE down. The two that scored are the only ones with an action head that does not depend on the anchor convention: flipped and transposed copies with a centred kernel in r2c2, and a dense linear head in r2c3. Read together, this suggests two problems: the world may remap actions in some way, and DONE takes over early. The evidence is weak, since 1/512 is close to noise. Round 3 follows the plan for after a first nonzero score: one near-copy of r2c2, three single-change variants (sample-heavy recipe, slower DONE, dense head plus longer credit), and two stacks that join the D4 head with the dense head.

### Round 4
Every trial outside the D4-symmetric-head family scored 0. Four trials scored 1/512: r2c2, r3c1 and r3c5 all contain the D4 head (flipped and transposed copies of learned features read through a centred symmetric kernel), and r2c3 is an everything stack. Training success is above 0 only for r3c1 (0.0013) and r2c3 (0.0005). So the agent almost never finishes an exact build, and the evidence is weak: one success in 512 is close to seed noise. If anything helps, it may be that the world's action layout is flipped or transposed relative to the description, and the D4 head lets each logit read mirrored positions. Within the D4 family, these changes scored 0 with one seed each: adding the dense head, 1 epoch, a DONE scale of 0.03, and gamma 0.99. A score must reach 2/512 to be selected over r2c2. This last round therefore keeps the D4 idea and varies its capacity and structure: a wider head, mirrors applied after local features, global context fed into the head, a deeper head, 3 epochs, and one stack of all of these.

## Trial it ended with
name: D4 late-mirror head
hypothesis: Mirrors after local features rather than before. A centred symmetric convolution first computes 32-channel footprint features from the full trunk features. The 8 D4 copies of those rich local features are then mixed by a 1x1 layer into per-type logits. Each logit can then read full local evidence at its mirrored positions, not just 8 reduced channels, which should fit a flipped or transposed action layout better. Refuted if dev and training success are both 0.

Return a JSON object: "verdict" ("yes", "partly" or "no") and "evidence" (at most 80 words, quoting the text and
naming the round it comes from).

reply.evidence: The text never says the target channels in the observation are shifted. Round 3 only guesses that "the world may remap actions in some way". Round 4 says "the world's action layout is flipped or transposed relative to the description". That is a mirror or transpose of the action layout, not a 4-row wrap-around shift of the target, missing, extra and height channels toward higher y. The final trial keeps the same flip/transpose idea. Wrong change, wrong place.
